newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese must foot Japan Railways debt - Mitsuzuka.
newsitem.headline: Japanese must foot Japan Railways debt - Mitsuzuka.

text.p: The Japanese people will have to foot the bill for 23 trillion yen ($203 billion) in debt still left from the privatisation of Japan Railways (JR) 10 years ago, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Saturday.

"The burden will be about 200,000 yen ($1,800) per citizen," Mitsuzuka said. "We are going to look at all possible alternatives to raise this money and we hope to settle the issue by around November or the beginning of December, before we start to look at the budget," he said on a news programme on the Fuji Television network.
Mitsuzuka said that of the 28 trillion yen ($247 billion) in debt still left, five trillion ($44 billion) would be covered by selling off Japan Railways' real estate and stock holdings.
The remaining 23 trillion would have to come from either the government's existing funds or from establishing a new tax, he said.
"We cannot issue any government debt to cover this, and I don't think we can have too big an expectation for the now-privatised JR companies to contribute to paying back the debt," Mitsuzuka said.
State-run Japan Railways was broken up in 1987 into seven private railway companies.
